'Twould be sublime tragedy if the men of America became so nearsighted as to see only some "high standard of living" envisioned for them by government, guild or custom, and, striving to hold on to that synthetic thing, lost all that was real by losing this war. In the safety of America, from the comfort of an overstuffed chair, with our stomachs full of good food, what right have we to prate of maintaining our "standards of living" when other Americans, racked with fever and gunshot wounds, living like savages with empty bellies in the brush on Luzon, are fighting to preserve for us an America in which every man may worship the God of his choosing, marry the woman of his heart, and out of his own courage, ability and willingness to work, achieve his own conception of a "high living standard!" All of us, as a Nation; each of us, as an individual, must discard glasses which distort our vision or cast a tint, too rosy or too dark, over the embattled scene. With clear, sharp-focused, long range vision we can shorten the journey over that hard road, through fog and storm, that stretches ahead to Victory.

Members of the National Rifle Association of America are ready to act when they hear the statement, "There ought to be a law!" They know from past experiences that someone, either deliberately or unwittingly, wants to legislate away one of the basic individual liberties of the American way of life. They know, too, that more often than not it involves the right of reputable citizens to keep and bear arms for lawful purposes. Too often gun owners and shooter-sportsmen are accused of hindering a visionary solution to the problems of law-enforcement, crime, or accidental shootings. Because they oppose overly restrictive firearms legislation, they are charged with being against everything - of taking the negative approach. This is not true! It is a fact that most proposed firearms legislation today takes the wrong approach. It is aimed at regulating the firearm rather than the person who handles it improperly or who uses it for unlawful purposes. Intelligent Americans will agree that under today's conditions guidelines must be established for the use of firearms in some areas. Nevertheless, this guidance must be based on reason and understanding, not on emotional reaction or misinformation. It is true that law-enforcement officers sometimes have difficulty in accomplishing the arrest and conviction of law-breakers. We appreciate their enthusiastic efforts in the public interest and recognize the problem. However, the desire to see our laws enforced is not justification for any proposed legislation which circumvents due process of law in order to obtain convictions more easily or which can make an unwitting violator of a prudent, law-abiding citizen. It is true that a small percentage of our population uses firearms for illegal purposes. We abhor this situation but believe that firearms legislation is of insufficient value in the prevention of crime to justify the inevitable restrictions which such legislation places upon law-abiding citizens. No law will prevent a gangster or other dangerous criminal from securing and using firearms. The positive approach is severe penalties for the commission of a crime while armed with a firearm and prohibiting the possession of firearms by convicted criminals. It is true that some gun accidents occur because individuals are careless or because they are ignorant of proper gun handling. We believe that gun accidents are unnecessary but they cannot be prevented by passing a law. The real answer to the problem of gun accidents and the positive approach to its solution is firearms education. Members of the National Rifle Association, more than any other group, are doing something about this problem. Millions of young people have been taught firearms safety and proper gun handling in the NRA Junior Shooting Program. More than a million novice hunters have learned gun safety in an NRA Hunter Safety Course during recent years. The ultimate responsibility for bad legislation cannot rest upon those who make the laws if individual voting Americans are indifferent or silent before the threat to deprive them of their guns and shooting. Those members of NRA who give of their time and effort to study the problems which create proposed gun laws and to assist lawmakers in separating the good gun legislation from the bad are rendering a true service for the gun owners and shooter-sportsmen of America. We salute them because they are taking the positive approach.

In the coming months - as we move toward the critical Congressional elections where pro-Second Amendment majorities in the U.S. Senate and House of Representatives hang in the balance - expect to see a big lie campaign led by New York City Mayor Michael Bloomberg, joined by urban machine politicians, federal career bureaucrats and anti-gun blue-state governors. The campaign centers around the fraudulent notion that the freedom residents enjoy in states such as Florida, Idaho or New Mexico is the cause of armed criminal violence in places such as New York City, Chicago, Boston or Washington, D.C. - jurisdictions boasting the most repressive "gun control" laws in the nation. Bloomberg, in a declaration of war on millions of law-abiding Americans elsewhere in the nation, defined his big lie in a radio address that came in the wake of the cold-blooded murders of two NYPD officers. Police identified one accused killer as a drug user, drug dealer and fugitive from justice who would have been - should have been - rotting away in a federal prison had existing federal laws been applied before he pulled the trigger. The second murder suspect has a long criminal record and is an admitted drug abuser. He is also being investigated in the shooting and wounding of another brave police officer just a month earlier. But in New York City, the accused cop killers repeatedly worked the system to their advantage. Yet, given that record of failure, Bloomberg shifted the blame from the accused criminals and his administration's ineptitude onto the backs of innocent citizens in other states, saying, "[g]uns are flooding into the City from states like Pennsylvania and Virginia, where people can buy guns easily and then sell them in cities like New York to those who cannot legally acquire them, including drug dealers and other dangerous criminals." You and I know that everything he describes is a crime under federal law, amounting to serial mega-felonies with mandatory penalties. There is nothing that has to do with criminals acquiring, transporting, possessing, transferring or using guns of any kind that can be made any more unlawful. Bloomberg - a billionaire Wall Street financier who reportedly used $80 million of his personal cash to pay for his election - was immediately joined in his big lie by New York Governor George Pataki, touted as a Republican presidential candidate. Anti-gun politicians like Bloomberg and Pataki just don't get it. The only thing that will stop criminals with or without guns is real enforcement - arrest, prosecution and mandatory jail time. But that's where the Bloombergs of this nation fail miserably. Bloomberg's New York City "enforcement of the law," according to a March 10, 2004, New York Times account, means "Only about 10 percent of felony arrests in Manhattan reach a court room ...." And of 100,000 misdemeanor cases, only 300 went to trial. Robert M. Morgenthau, Manhattan district attorney, blamed the decrease in cases going to trial on deep budget cuts that force prosecutors to accept plea bargains instead. The Times article quoted Queens District Attorney Richard A. Brown, saying that "there are already signs on our streets that criminals are becoming more brazen about dealing drugs and carrying weapons." Had New York City officials been prosecuting criminals like they should, repeat felons would not have been on the street free to kill. They're not enforcing tough laws on the books against criminals, yet they demand more gun laws targeting what innocent, good people do in exercising their Second Amendment rights. Just look at the dark years of the Clinton Administration when enforcement and prosecution were abandoned - a time when nearly 1 million fugitives, felons and drug dealers were not arrested and prosecuted even though they committed multiple felonies in breaking our nation's firearm laws. You can't "prevent" a violent criminal from violating the law unless you lock him up. Human beings possess free will, exercised for evil or good. And in our system of justice, the guilty should pay the price for the evil they inflict upon the innocent. That's what NRA stands for. Until Bloomberg and Pataki understand that principle, criminals will laugh at their misguided rhetoric all the way to the next crime scene. The truth is, when it comes to criminal trafficking, criminal possession and criminal use of any firearm, the laws are already on the books. The punishments mandated in that single federal law cover every armed, violent criminal in every corner of the nation. That's the truth Bloomberg and Pataki just don't get.

When I began this column in 1985, it was intended as an open forum where NRA members could contribute their ideas, suggestions and criticisms. This month's letter comes from a husband and wife NRA-Life Member team in Indiana, with eye towatd expanding NRA educational opportunities. Please keep your letters coming, and have a happy, safe 1986. Dear Mr. Arnett, My husband and I are both Life Members of the NRA and certainly welcome your open format for ideas and concerns. With the great proliferation of video cassette recorders, we believe it would be a tremendous asset if the NRA would take some of its instructional materials and concert them to VCR tapes. They could be offered to membership, educate the membership, their friends and family (who hopefully will become NRA members too). In this age of more people wanting guns for self-protection, the image of the NRA can only be enhanced by offering quality tapes for a better informed public. To allay any fears you may have that this is a "sales pitch" from a VCR tape company, assure you that my husband and I are not connected to this industry in any fashion. We're just devoted to NRA members who (we think) see a trend that is coming to American communications. We hope you'll consider this idea as you would any other suggestion for NRA's future. Please keep up the good work and thank you for giving us NRA members the opportunity to voice our concerns to other members. Mrs. C.L., Claypool, Ind. I welcome constructive criticism and agree that you have a very good idea. Video tapes do indeed seem to he an idea whose time has come and we certainly want to make use of them. Last fall for instance, our NRA Hunter Services and Public Education Divisions began a video-tape project in conjunction with the 3M Company. The result was two outstanding 55-minute hunting films - "Successful Whitetail Deer Hunting" and "Way of the Whitetail," both of which are now available from the NRA Video Service. We co-produced the videos with two goals in mind: Helping the American sportsman to become a better hunter through a detailed product, and helping to teach better hunting by channeling a portion of the proceeds of each video tape sale toward NRA's hunter education and clinic programs. The NRA Education and training Division also entered the video arena in 1981, producing three marksmanship training videos - "Rifle Shooting Fundamentals," "Pistol Shooting Fundamentals" and "Shotgun Shooting Fundamentals" - in conjunction with the Athletic Institute, the foremost producer and distributor of sports films in the world today. We also now offer our 24-minute, 16 mm film "The Kid Who Can't Miss," in three video formats as well. The NRA is exploring a number of possible video educational opportunities for 1986. A tape tentatively titled "Principles of Self Defense" may soon be offered for use with the NRA Voluntary Practical Firearms Program, where it would act as a primer on how to design a strategy to secure your home and self from criminal assault. We also are discussing with an independent producer the idea of NRA participating in a tape (and film) on the basics of teaching a young person to hunt, as well as a series of home videos on the "How To's" of hunting various game animals. Some of the projects we are considering would be aimed at large classes like schools and affiliated associations, while others would be more suited to home viewing or television broadcast. In all our video projects I might add we have placed as much emphasis on entertainment as we have on educational value. We want material that is lively and dynamic as well as instructive and informative. But video tapes - like any project - mean a considerable investment by the Association. They require everything from  hundreds of staff hours spent in production to coordination with marketing and promotional experts to having resources available to fulfill members orders. All of this means time - and money. The NRA wants - indeed we intend - to expand our video services just as we want to expand all our Association programs. We cannot accomplish this however, without coming up with the capital to finance these projects. As I am sure you are aware, the NRA has a modest dues increase slated tor April 1, the first increase in nine years. Look at the difference between your NRA now and a scant nine years ago. Nine years ago we had no aggressive public education program like our "I'm the NRA" campaign. We had no Voluntary Practical Firearms Program teaching principles of self defense. We did not publish an InSight magazine for our junior members, nor did we sponsor our North American Hunter Education Championship or our Young Hunter Qualification Awards. We formed our important Field Services Division in 1980 and have seen the number of NRA Field Reps go from less than a dozen to its current 21. Five years ago we founded our well-accepted Security Firearms Training Department that provides industry and private business the same firearms training experience we give America's police. We have expanded our involvement in the Law Enforcement Explorer program that each year teaches young men and women interested in police work the fundamentals of marksmanship and firearm safety. And, needless to say, we had no NRA Video Service like we started in 1985. Frankly, this entire column (and more) could be filled with many NRA programs and activities that have been developed in the last nine years. In a special section of this month's NRA magazines, these projects are shown and desribed much better than I could hope to detail in my column. Please look closely at the new NRA, at how it has grown and what it has accomplished in such a short time. I think you'll agree that the dues increase nine years ago certainly proved its worth, just as this 1986 increase will in its own right. You and your husband have shared with us a viable idea for increasing NRA's clout through the video-tape medium, and we genuinely appreciate your suggestion. We hope you will be as excited and enthusiastic as we are about promoting the new NRA and thank you for all your loyal support.

Celebrating NRA's 116th anniversary, we just concluded our Annual Meetings in Reno, Nev., and by any standard this get-together was a thundering success. Running from April 21-28 and including, among other things, an Awards Luncheon, an Opening Session featuring some of our nation's most prominent political leaders, the Annual Meeting of Members, the Members Banquet, NRA Board and Committee Meetings and various conferences, workshops, sessions and exhibits, thousands upon thousands of NRA members had an opportunity to see their Association in action. Voters numbering 2,132 picked up their credentials for Saturday's Meeting of Members, over 2,000 fire on our airgun range, 1,300 enjoyed a magnificent banquet on Saturday evening, listening to U.S. House Majority Leader Tom Foley and 18,000 visited the Exhibit Hall. And a special salute to the 200-plus certified instructors attending our first National Instructors Conference. As only .001% of our members heard NRA's officers report on April 25, I think it proper that my remarks be repeated in this column. Thank you Wayne LaPierre, Executive Director of ILA and Gary Anderson, Executive Director of General Operations for those outstanding reports. A magnificent record of accomplishment from legislation and politics, through education and training to competition and hunting. To these achievements our Treasurer, Bill Binswanger, will present a bright financial picture which includes the largest gross membership income ever produced in one month, February's record $6,389,881. At the close of April's accounting period our Membership Division Director, Jim Land, will report 2,803,527 total paid members - a net increase of 11,000 members over April, 1986. Most significantly, our members renewed at an unprecedented rate of almost 77% during 1986 and that figure is holding for the first three months of this year. An item that is sure to bring smiles to your faces is that of a 25% reduction in direct mail to our members for this entire year as compared to last. My friends, that is 11 million fewer times we will help clog your mailbox this year. This was accomplished by sticking to priorities, merging and purging our lists and doing a better job of targeting. But enough facts and figures. You can read all of this and more in our written reports and in our magazines. What won't appear there is the depth of my heartfelt thanks to you, our membership, to an active, courageous Board of Directors, and to a dedicated, fiercely loyal professional staff. Consider the challenges. Changes in dues, leadership, membership promotions and public relations operations. We have conquered those but look what remains ahead: a changing society, shrinking game habitat, a difficult political climate and a wealthier, more aggressive enemy - the anti-gun movement. You've seen Sarah Brady and listened to her sympathizers in the media. The anti-gunners don't care about legislations anymore. We've beaten them so many times on the facts and the issues that they've decided their only hope is to discredit you and me -  the NRA. Their motive is simple and obvious: Convince the people of this great nation that the NRA is the enemy. Weaken our stature and their legislative goals become attainable. Lately, due to an unfortunate alliance between the anti-gun press and some misguided NRA members their hopes skyrocketed. Let me quote the Syracuse, N.Y. Herald Journal. The headline is "NRA Split, Maybe Distraction Will Soften Hard Line." "Perhaps if the NRA is distrusted by philosophic divisions and internal bickering in its ranks it will have less time to court our representatives in Congress or to think of new ways to make it easier for people to kill each other because of lay ineffective or non-existent gun control legislation. [A former employee...described the rift in the Association as 'bitter and destructive.' With any luck, his depiction of the situation will turn out to be prophetic rather than merely the paranoid ramblings of a disenchanted few. Men and women of NRA, we will not let his prophecy become reality. One hundred and sixteen years of a proud, honorable, and, yes, famous tradition will assert itself and overcome our enemies. Sarah Brady, Chief McNamara and the rest will not go unanswered. We will expose their campaign what it is. We will tell NRA's story - we will speak of our philosophy, our people and our programs. We have men and women, boys and girls, served this nation proudly and with great distinction for all of these years. And what better year in which to tell that story and reaffirm our commitment to the preservation of individual freedoms than in this, the 200th anniversary of the Constitution of the United States. NRA has established an unmatched record of achievement in the defense of your rights. As we meet today for the first time in this great state of Nevada with the eyes of our Country upon us, let us go forth from this hall united in our caused, strengthened in our friendships and dedicated to the defeat of any individual or organization who dares to attack us, our Association or our Country. Ladies and gentleman, you are the NRA. Stand proud and thank God for the privilege of living in America. With your help I promise to continue to uphold and promote the God-given rights upon which this Country of ours was founded - Thank you. Despite the fervent hopes of the anti-gunners, some national media and a few disgruntled NRA members, the Annual Meeting of Members was conducted in magnificent fashion by President Jim Reinke. All who approached the microphone had an opportunity to express their views and, where necessary, hear them debated long and loudly. For eight hours reporters saw democracy in action and left the hall with an increased respect for the strength and vitality of your Association. All in all, a most successful 116th birthday.

School is out! There go the kids! Where are they going? What are they going to get into before the school bell rings again? A few of the luckier ones will go into summer camps, into the congested but wholesome activities of some Boys' Club, or will take up their share of the work load on the farm. Most of them are going into the city streets, out to the city dumps, off into the suburban wood lots and fields. Some of them, giving vent to normal, healthy, animal spirits, unguided by sympathetic adult experience, will drown in forbidden swimming holes. Some will rush under the crushing wheels of modern traffic. Some, seeking the acclaim of their mates, will transgress the grownups' rules of propriety and will join the list of juvenile "delinquents". Some will venture, untrained, unwarned, to play with forbidden weapons. There will be accidental shootings. And for every such incident there will be a community reaction against the sale and use of firearms. What are you going to do about it, Mister? These kids, you know, are the America of tomorrow. You may be childless but you have got to live with these youngsters and their parents - not only tomorrow but today. Do you want to pay for a bigger police force? Do you want more antifirearms laws? Do you want to lie, sleepless, looking into the black night at the drawn, parchment-white features of a kid who ran under your car in the traffic stream? Don't you want to spend your old age in a nation governed by clear-headed, straight-thinking, courageous younger men? You can't safely pass the buck, Mister. Maybe you can't contribute much to the local Boys' Club. Maybe you can't serve as a Scout Master. But two things you can do. As a citizen you can demand of your city fathers that they furnish more off-the-street play areas and supervised junior recreation programs. As a sportsman you can take one kid into your gun room and give him the greatest thrill of his young life while you tell him the story of your guns, how they work and how the real sportsman always handles firearms safely, sanely, and expertly. You can take one kid out to the range or into some safe spot in the woods or fields and teach him how to shoot. You can prod your local sportsmen's club into instituting a real junior program of instruction in shooting, conservation, sportsmanship, that will contribute mightily to the reduction in traffic accidents, shooting accidents, swimming accidents and "juvenile delinquency." Perhaps you can even awaken your community to a knowledge of the fact that the very term "juvenile delinquency" is a phrase coined by adults to cover up their own delinquency in neglecting the youngsters they have brought into the world! School's out. The kids are spreading out everywhere. They are getting into everything. If they get into trouble it's your fault, Mister!

Violence in America takes its strongest news media form in The Washington Post Company's outbursts against firearms. Few media can match the virulence of this organization's anti-gun campaigning on the air and in print. So it is interesting to note in passing that not all of its newsmen practice what The Washington Post and its anti-gun television station, WTOP, constantly preach. A Washington Post reporter was arrested some time ago on a charge of carrying a concealed firearm "within a few blocks of the White House," as the Post is fond of saying sinisterly in other gun connections. He got off with a small fine, his newspaper published a very small news item about it, and that presumably was that. More recently, Washington, D.C., police responded to a midnight call about gunfire in the 1500-unit Van Ness Apartments and arrested a newsman for the Post's WTOP-TV. As the Post reported it, the newsman fired a .357 Magnum revolver "several times" in his backyard. As another Washington paper reported it, neighbors counted "up to 18 rounds." That's a lot of shooting in a dense residential area. The TV newsman explained that he was upset by the death of his father three weeks earlier, "had never owned a gun and never wanted one," but brought the .357 revolver back from Richmond, Va., because it had belonged to his dad. He apologized on a TV newscast that evening. Washington police allowed him to forfeit $25 collateral and, though the revolver was unregistered, marked the case closed. Federal authorities said they were "looking into the matter," as it involved acquiring a firearm in another State and transporting it across State lines.

When the U.S. Attorney General tells the "NRA to get lost," then America's gun owners better take it as a hurricane-force anti-gun storm brewing. And when this country's new FBI Director says he'll support the "strongest firearms legislations," then Second Amendment supporters had better realize we're now up against a federal anti-gun police force. And when the President of the United States goes out of his way to ask Congress to send him anti-gun legislation to sign, then hunters, shooters and self-defense advocates should see the handwriting's already on the walls in very high places. And when some of the most powerful enemies of constitutionally protected firearm ownership tell the press they foresee clear sailing ahead, you'd better believe our foes think this nation's pro-gun defenses are ready to crumble. Is the fall of 1993 going to make history as the fall of the Second Amendment and its NRA defenders? It's in your hands. And here's why. Intense legislative attacks now underway call for broad ranging semi-auto bans, "proof of need" gun licensing, gun registration complete with fingerprinting, firearm purchase limits, bans and taxes on ammo and even restrictions on hunter access to public lands. And that's just for openers. The anti-gun forces plan to take every thing they can get, and, according to one notorious gun-hating lawmaker, this could mean a total ban on firearm ownership by anyone except the police or military. So get ready for the battle of a lifetime. Because for the first time, we're up against the breadth of the Washington, DC power structure, plus the media, plus the FBI, plus whoever else is waiting in the wings. We need you to call and write your U.S. representatives and U.S. senators right now! Tell them you want real crime control measures instead of senseless attacks on your Second Amendment rights. And if you possibly can, make a contribution to NRA's Institute for Legislative Action and renew or upgrade your NRA membership. Do it now. Because it may be now or never.

Each of us in the shooting game is intensely interested in seeing our sport attract more individuals who feel as we do about it. The message below appeared in this magazine in 1938 as an advertisement of the Sporting Powder Division of the Hercules Powder Company, Inc., of Wilmington, Delaware. I believe you will agree with it, as well as the comments on our part, and urge you to spread the good word - by deed. "You know and we know that rifle shooting provides more fun, and more valuable mental and physical training, at less cost, than any other sport. It is to the advantage of those interested in the game to make these facts known; because more shooters will mean more good shots, more competition, and more enjoyment for everybody. "Devotees of rifle shooting include men and women, boys and girls, of all physical types. Persons below the average in size and strength are under no handicap; physical bulk and muscularity are in themselves no advantage. It is coordination and control of body, mind, and nerves that count; and gradually, without undue fatigue or strain, practice with the rifle develops these qualities. It teaches precision, carefulness of details, accurate observation, and the priceless ability to relax. It quickens the eye and steadies the hand. In fact, rifle shooting endows its followers with exactly those attributes that are most valuable in the usual walks of life: the calm assurance that results from steady nerves - the feeling of confidence in emergencies that comes from a sense of power held in reserve. "However, riflemen would be the last to concede that the desire for physical and mental well-being accounts for the irresistible lure of their sport. These are by-products attained without effort, and often without giving them a thought. No sport indulged in primarily to promote health can claim a large following. To become truly popular, it must meet certain basic human desires. Let us see what the main qualifications of the ideal sport are and to what extent these are possessed by rifle shooting. "In the first place, we seek in sport complete absorption in an interest outside of our routine activities - something that will make us temporarily forget our daily cares and worries and send us back to our regular duties refreshed and stimulated. We like to pit our skill in friendly competition against others whose ability corresponds to ours; or we may be satisfied to compete against our own previous performances. We look for elements of interest that carry beyond the actual indulgence in the sport itself, that provide food for thought and study, and a fruitful source of fascinating discussion wherever two or more of the initiates are gathered together. Above all. many of us want our recreation mixed with good fellowship and zestful social intercourse with others who share our enthusiasms. "A sport that can fulfill all these desires is obviously at the forefront of man's diversions; and to those who have fallen under its spell, it is equally obvious that in rifle shooting we find complete fulfillment of these desires. On the score of good fellowship, particularly, the rifleman enjoys advantages undreamed of by followers of other pastimes. With him, at least, the boasted democracy of sport is an actuality. On the rifle-range the bank director rubs shoulders with the farm hand; the corporation president freely fraternizes with labor. Social and financial barriers are non-existent. Men judge each other for what they are. Firm and lasting friendships are formed between those whose ordinary walks are worlds apart, and whose paths would not cross anywhere in America save on the rifle-range. "Certainly there is no conspiracy to keep the fun of rifle shooting a secret. Rifle clubs are hospitable to the stranger. Their members are cordially willing to help beginners with advice and instruction. Dues and initiate fees raise no formidable barriers to those of modest income. After a small initial investment in equipment, the cost of shooting is gratifyingly moderate. But the many solid claims to the nation's leisure hours that rifle shooting presents serve to emphasize that there are not as many adherents as these claims warrant. If those of us who find such keen pleasure on the range are not exactly secretive about it, perhaps we do not make enough noise about. Let's not be too prone to mind our own business when meet the fellow who is happily married to some other sport. After all, he won't know what sport is until he snuggles a rifle stock up to his cheek." When this message was published almost 17 years ago the National Rifle Association of America had fewer than 50,00 members. Today there are almost six times that number. This is solid evidence that some 'noise' has been made about shooting and that those who have tried it, like it. Everyone is agreed that one of the goals of each of us is for a bigger and stronger NRA. We can all aid in achieving this goal by making a noise about guns and gunning. Whether it be about rifle, handgun, or shotgun shooting; hunting; collecting old or new guns; or gunsmithing, NRA membership provides services and answers. At this season of the year, there is a specific way of making this noise - it is by giving an NRA membership as a Christmas gift to someone who you know will benefit from being a member, and receiving The American Rifleman each month (see page 53).

In all the years I have been with NRA, I have never been so proud of our membership or felt so humble in your presence as during my travels in the months and weeks before this election. NRA. We are a solemn partnership; a bond between individual Americans who are always willing to fight for Freedom, and those of us privileged to work on your behalf on the frontlines of liberty. We will never let you down, just as you will never cease to do the most important part - petitioning government and communicating with others to energize the majority of Americans who agree with us. Poll after poll show that a huge percentage of our fellow citizens believe they have a Right to Keep and Bear Arms. That is why gun-banning politicians are talking our talk, while they continue to walk their oppressive walk. At one campaign stop, an NRA member said, "I wish Chuck Heston were here." I didn't even think about it when I answered, "He is with us." When I looked around at all those wonderful people I saw Freedom fighters - the heart and soul of our uniquely American culture of liberty. Chuck Heston's spirit was with them in their passion to protect our traditions of Freedom. At every single stop, NRA Institute for Legislative Action Executive Director Chris Cox and I were deeply touched by the trust, the commitment and love of NRA members for our organization and our cause. Everywhere, people responded with contributions for the battles ahead, many expressing similar thoughts, "I know NRA will be needing this." One common theme ran like a wide, strong river: people are angry that radical political agendas have melded with equally radical media coverage. "Coverage" is certainly the right word. As in giving credence to a blatant lie. The self-appointed "watchdogs" in the media are now running with the wolves to take down our Freedom like never before. We Americans are idealists. We hope that politicians will be honest. We hope that there is such a concept as media neutrality; and that a politician's record would define his views. When a candidate for high office can "cover" his entire record with a totally false claim, and never once be challenged by the mainstream media, something precious has died in America. With the advent of the Internet and of conservative talk radio, the corporate media elites have become more and more transparent. Perhaps that explains their rabid transition from any sense of fairness to their outward expressions of hatred for basic, old-time American values. Decent, ordinary Americans find their truth from a remarkable array of sources in talk radio and on the Internet-sources far more reliable than the elite national media. Hard digging bloggers have filled the void of real reporting in the old media. Former NBC anchor Tom Brokaw, interviewed on the Hugh Hewlett radio show, referred to blogs as "cancerous," saying, "I'm a free speech absolutist, but I think that at the same time, we have to have free speech in some kind of a context." (emphasis added) In 1996, Brokaw said, "I also believe strongly that the Internet works best when there are gatekeepers. When there are people making determinations and judgments about what information is relevant and factual and useful." Those chilling thoughts give an insight into battles we will be called upon to fight in the near future - battles to save not just the Second Amendment, but the First Amendment. The two are entwined as the essential keys to our liberty. One does not exist without the other. With Barack Obama's campaign, we saw a total disregard for open and free speech. Broadcasters that ran truthful, accurate NRA Political Victory Fund ads were threatened with legal action. Internet sites critical of that candidate were attacked and shut down by the massive use of spam buttons.Talk radio shows were inundated with threatening calls demanding that guests be denied the opportunity to speak. Truth - just plain facts - were labeled as "smears." As a result of the political shifts in Congress, these attacks on open discourse will be expanded. There will be a major effort to "regulate" the Internet. And there will be direct attacks on the NRA as an American institution. Given these threats, individual NRA members are asking what they can do to help us safeguard the future of our Freedom. The immediate answer is to sign up at least one new member. Our power is in our numbers, but it is more than that. NRA members possess something critically important, a willingness to fight no matter what the odds. If each of us does that one thing- sign up one patriotic American who cares as much about Freedom as we do - we can be prepared to win victories in the uncertain future. And I promise you this: in the coming months and years, as individual NRA members fighting together through our great institution, we will be victorious. Our greatest strength is you. Together with the partnership that is the NRA, we will hold the line against every threat from every quarter. Attacks on the Second Amendment will be stopped. Attacks on the First Amendment will be checked. Together, we are the one force in America that can provide the fortitude to keep Americans a free people.

Back in the days when men still remembered how much had been the cost of American liberty the Fourth of July was a day of great celebration. No one played golf, there were no stadiums to seat thousands of umpire-baiting, but otherwise inactive, spectators at professional athletic tourneys. Some people were injured and a few were killed by the excesses of the celebrants' zeal, but the casualty list was only a tiny fraction of the traffic toll taken by the automobile in these days of "safe and sane" observance. "Observance" is the proper term nowadays rather than "celebration." For some years "sanity" in matters pertaining to patriotism, has been the fetish of our leaders of public thought. Indeed, one may recall without too much groping in memory's caverns the period - after the last war - when intellectuals, from Senators to school teachers, warned the rising generation of Americans that "patriotism" was a dangerous drug used by the munitions trust to drive men into the insanity of defending their independence. "Flag waving," as it referred to waving the American flag, became unfashionable during this period. The debunkers were hard at work proving that George Washington, Patrick Henry and Abraham Lincoln were just ordinary mortals and that school-boys had no more reason to respect and revere them than other human beings-such as, for instance, Messrs. Marx, Lenin or Trotsky. Our literature turned from the inspirational exposition of the fine and great things accomplished by the builders of America to the "sane" objective and too often half-baked discussion of theoretical methods of changing things having their root in unchangeable human nature. With the debunking of the old American heroes came a natural discrediting of the principles and ideals which had guided our founding fathers. Liberty became fouled with license, independence confused with disrespect. The idea that the citizen owed something to the Nation was subverted into the idea that the Nation owed everything to the citizen. The great school of "hand-it-over-to-the-hold-up-man-then-yell-for-the-police" began to take the place of the ancient Anglo-Saxon doctrine that a man's home is his castle. But, peculiarly, while the leaders of the new thought in America decried "flag waving" as applied to the red, white and blue of the Stars and Stripes, they saw nothing amiss in the fluttering aloft of the red and white of the Hammer and Sickle! "May Day" might be properly "celebrated" though the Fourth of July should only be "observed." All who thought such a situation a bit out of place in America were promptly labeled "old fogey", "reactionary", "tory". Now, on the verge of a great and bitter war, we reap the harvest we ourselves have sown. The debunkers of "flag waving" (American style) have emerged in their true color-red. Their mentally immature and disillusioned playmates have become the loudest exponents of "old fashioned" patriotism and flag waving. They are hurt and befuddled because the generation which they raised to sneer at old-fashioned Americanism are now slow to understand why they should "celebrate" the Fourth of July instead of having a "sane observance" of the day. Fortunately, the great mass of Americans of this generation, as of the older generations, are fundamentally sound and sensible. They are fundamentally patriotic because patriotism is common sense. On this Fourth of July, 1941, may we have a return to a good old-fashioned American flag-waving, "I'm-proud-to-be-an-American" celebration. It will serve to sweep out a lot of cob-webs from the minds of Americans-and it will perhaps encourage a physical house-cleaning of those termites who prefer to wave the Red Flag. "Our Objective: Organize strife and combat groups; formulate plans for disarming police, loyal troops and loyal fighting workmen; destroy, when unable to capture all weapons which loyal proletariats might use." Communist doctrine from The Congressional Record.

Too many Americans think of communism, fascism, and other catch-phrase 'isms' as something material, something physical, which can be created or destroyed by financial expenditure and by the use of force. In the American language 'communism' is synonymous with Russia; 'Nazi-ism' with Germany; 'fascism' with Italy and Spain. The current trend in our thinking is 'defeat Russia and you defeat communism,' 'destroy the Politburo and the Cominform and you destroy communism.' It isn't that simple. Germany and Italy lie defeated. Hitler and Mussolini lie destroyed. Nazi-ism and fascism are not dead. The simple fact is that communism, like all the other isms, including Americanism, is a state of mind - an ideal. Ideals cannot he bought or sold. They cannot be born or killed by force. If Americanism is to survive then all those ideas which make up the American ideal must be bred and nourished. All those ideas which undermine the American ideal must he rendered sterile or he killed. Americans have always worried about the effect on our democracy of 'the professional military state of mind.' Authors and orators have preached the dangers of the development of a military state - a government controlled by military ideas. It is high time that we give some thought and some publicity to the 'professional police state of mind.' Communism, Nazi-ism, fascism are (or were) police states-not military states. Steadily through the past generation we have encouraged the development of a professional police class in America. We have fostered the idea that crime is a highly specialized subject beyond the comprehension of the average citizen and beyond his ability to do anything about. In ever-increasing numbers the local policeman has been 'sent to school' to learn efficient police methods but also to subconsciously absorb the professional police state of mind from a few state or federal professionals. More and more has the public prosecutor, the most vocal and highly trained representative of the law enforcement group, found his way into the legislative, executive, and judicial branches of local, state, and federal government. Whatever has gone amiss in our social or economic life, we have tried to correct, not by intelligent study and education, but by passing another law. In most cases those laws have been urged for passage by present or former policemen or prosecutors. Particularly notable has been the willingness of State Legislatures to place in the hands of State Game Commissions the right to promulgate the laws and regulations which the Commissions then interpret and enforce. For an enforcement officer to be able to make his own laws is the acme of the police state psychology. The police state of mind, necessary forebearer of the police state, is more of an element in American life than most Americans realize. We do not believe that any American police official is today conscious of the potential viciousness of the trend or is anything but opposed to the police state idea. We believe that in this, as in other matters affecting the well being of our citizens and the future of our democracy, the dangerous drift in our national state of mind is due entirely to the mental and political laziness of a large portion of the American electorate. The drive for antifirearms laws is a typical example of the police state of mind. It is no mere coincidence that such laws fit so perfectly into the communist program for 'disarming the bourgeoisie.' Communism is, paradoxically, both the father and the child of the police state. America needs to return to that state of mind envisioned by Thomas Jefferson when he said "that government is best which governs least."

Pastor Martin Niemoller made the following statement at the time of his arrest by the Gestapo in 1937: "In Germany, they came first for the communists, and I didn't speak up because I wasn't a communist. Then, they came for the Jews, and I didn't speak up because I wasn't a Jew. Then, they came for the trade unionists, and I didn't speak up because I wasn't a trade unionist. Then, they came for the Catholics. I didn't speak up because I was a Protestant. Then, they came for me and by that time no one was left to speak up." To paraphrase for my purposes: "In America, they came first for the machine guns, and I didn't speak up because I wasn't a machine gunner. Then, they came for the handguns, and I didn't speak up because I wasn't a handgunner. Then, they came for the semi-autos, and I didn't speak up because I wasn't a semi-auto owner. Then, they came for the competitor, and I didn't speak up because I was a hunter. Then, they came for me, and by that time no one was left to speak up." This column is directed to those of you who have questioned NRA's opposition to the wave of semi-automatic gun bans sweeping the country in the wake of the Stockton schoolyard killings. Your apparent fear is the damage you perceive being done to our image by such resistance. Let's try to put this very serious matter in perspective. One concerned member wrote that he "would gladly give up one of my guns if it meant keeping all the others." I explained that the anti-gunners were not offering him this option, but only taking each piece of his modest collection until nothing is left. Evidence of this truth abounds. Randolph Ryan, writing in the Boston Globe, Feb 5, states: "The aim of gun control is not to ban gun ownership but to restrict it sensibly, beginning with meaningful controls on the worst weapons." He goes on to say that the politician must "go after the killer weapons, free-fire automatics and, eventually, concealables." The London Economist, in claiming that "Britain's gun laws are now too lax," said that "Most important is the stricter control of shotguns." The Washington Post, in one of its almost weekly tirades against NRA, attacked us for supporting the law-abiding citizen's right to own handguns. Asks the Post, "But how easily should anyone - trained or untrained, sane or insane, with or without past criminal convictions - be able to buy a handgun?" And Dan Ruth, Chicago Sun-Times columnist, responding to NRA Director James Zangrilli's charge that Ruth was really attacking all guns in his column on Ak 47s. said "You are absolutely right. I was indeed expressing my 'true feelings' with respect to eliminating all forms of firearms from society." Your high power rifles have already been excluded from the Olympic Games. Licensed and registered machine gun owners, without a criminal stain on their record for over half a century, can no longer purchase newly manufactured machine guns. Handguns have been banned in Washington, D.C. New York City, Chicago, Morton Grove, Oak Park and now Wilmette, Ill. Yesterday, Feb 22, 1989, Cleveland adopted this ordinance. "Any assault weapon is hereby declared to be contraband and shall be seized and disposed of . ." Cleveland's definition of "assault weapon" won't fit yours! A New York City councilor has proposed an ordinance to ban all semi-auto rifles and shotguns, regardless of style, magazine capacity, etc. And Sen. Daniel Moynihan, from the same state, fathers a bill to ban .25 and .32 cal. ammunition. His rationale? If Congress could ban armor-piercing ammo, why not other kinds? So tell me that all we have to do to appease the enemy's insatiable appetite for our firearms is to throw him a few black, plastic-stocked, non-traditional looking semi-automatics and we can go back to arguing whether the .30-'06 or the .270 is the most versatile caliber. The furor over the tragedy in Stockton, Calif. overlooks many pertinent facts, chiefly the failure of the criminal justice system. But another point I have not seen made is that any killer familiar with firearms could have murdered just as many children with a bolt-action rifle, a lever-action carbine, a pump-action shotgun, or for that matter, an automobile. In 63 years the state of California has gone from no waiting period for the purchase of handguns to one day then three days then five days and finally 15 days. During this same period California's violent crime rate has multiplied faster than the national average! How can this sorry record be used as proof that waiting periods will affect criminal misuse of semi-automatic rifles? Before non-supporters of so-called "assault rifles" toss these semi-automatics out of the sleigh to appease the pursuing wolves, insist that the editors who predict a safer, saner society with the absence of such fire arms bring evidence before the nation's legislators and courts to justify their contentions. We deserve the same treatment afforded the victims of eminent domain proceedings. Only after the public need for such action is proved beyond the shadow of a doubt can the property be taken. The burden of proof weighs heavily on those who would confiscate our real estate. And this same burden of proof is the least we demand of those who would deprive us of our personal property and our civil rights. This isn't England, thank God, where the same Economist article quoted went on to say, "In town or country, the onus should be on the would-be gunner to prove his point, not, as now, the other way around." The National Rifle Association of America is not defending a specific firearm. We are defending individual rights, constitutional guarantees and due process of law. This is the reality of NRA. This must be our image.

With increasing intensity, conservationists and preservationists have engaged in a war of words over the future of the world's game. Most conservationists favor maintaining a wildlife balance by means of limited, regulated hunting. Most preservationists would ban all hunting by human beings and "let nature take its course." Preservationists regard hunting as uncivilized and out-of-date. Hunting conservationists tend to view preservationists as impractical idealists who ought to be 100% vegetarians. Upon the dusty playing field of this fine global controversy there has now lumbered majestically perhaps the ultimate question or issue on the subject: What to do about elephants? One of the largest concentrations of elephants still in the wild or natural state exists in the Tsavo National Park, in Kenya, East Africa. The number, in an area about the size of Massachusetts, has been estimated at 25,000 and up. Under normal conditions - something which is in itself a world rarity these day s -an average three-ton elephant spends two-thirds of every day eating, presumably to keep up his weight. He is strictly a vegetarian, which probably scores points for him with the preservationists. Even when trampling a few natives or a white hunter, he refrains from sampling the result. But he consumes 100 to 150 pounds of vegetation a day, most of it stripped from trees which then die. When it comes to clearing forest, the elephant is nature's own bulldozer. The insatiable hunger of elephants has, it now develops, changed much of the Tsavo National Park from forest to grassland in recent years. Last year, nature added a crusher. The rains were far below normal. Searing droughts dried up water holes. Vegetation crispened and withered. The elephant herds ranged farther than usual but began to go thirsty and hungry. Soon their ground courses could be tracked by flocks of ready vultures overhead, waiting to prey on the fallen giants. Scenes of wilderness horror ensued. As Los Angeles Times correspondent Stanley Meisler wrote from Kenya: "There can be few more terrible sights in nature than that of a once magnificent elephant dead in a drought." In this instance, as in others involving North American game such as deer, the preservationists are stoutly defending the right of an elephant to die slowly and miserably of thirst and hunger. One of the senior game wardens in the area and a research director in ecology whose program is financed by the Ford Foundation both take the "leave it to nature" position and oppose any hunting to reduce the elephant herds and quicken the decimation. They say only the fittest survive as it is, and resist proposals of scientific "cropping" by regulated hunts. Meanwhile elephants have died by the hundred and possibly by the thousand. The situation, sad from any viewpoint, leaves unanswered questions. Elephants arc the largest packages of "meat-on-the-hoof" on earth. Should they be prey for vultures or food for natives? Is it kinder to let them die by slow degrees or by instant bullets? What is really best for the ecology? Anyone is free to reach his own answers.

I am frequently asked, "What does NRA have to offer citizens concerned about self-protection from criminal attack?" NRA is launching a campaign to reform restrictive gun laws that deny the means of self-defense to millions of Americans. This campaign is in part a response to letters like the following. Gentlemen, I'm a young, married woman who in home alone alot in the evening while my husband is working overtime. Recently, my girlfriend's husband (age 25) got shot to death for no apparent reason, he left behind a wife and a 3-year-old son. It has been one crime after another, it seems like nobody cares any more and that people aren't protected enough. I think now is the time for me to learn more about NRA. It would be greatly appreciated and maybe I'll even feel a little safer again. L.F., Forest Park, Ill. Self-defense is a fundamental right. Yet this right has been tortuously attacked by gun prohibitionists who devise laws that deny citizens the means to protect themselves and their loved ones from violent, predatory, criminal attack. Literally hundreds of requests for legal aid pour into NRA headquarters annually from members who, in legitimately using fire-arms for personal protection, later find themselves caught in the juggernaut of confusing, conflicting, and unfair gun laws. And while some citizens embrace the adage, "I'd rather be tried by twelve than earned by six," the legal system is a costly, arduous, lengthy and often arbitrary recourse when it comes to restoring gun rights. You may be fortunate enough to live in an area where family and friends can travel safely at any time of the day or night. In your town or city, locks on doors may be an after thought - not a first line of defense. In major metropolitan areas like Chicago or New York, though, many citizens live in perpetual fear: fear of neighbors, or strangers and of crime. For these people, barred and bolted windows and doors have transformed their homes and apartments into virtual prisons. For them, the right to self-defense is not an abstract, philosophical issue - the right to keep and bear arms is not just a piece of constitutional history. For these afflicted citizens, and for the estimated six million victims of crime in America each year, the right to keep and bear arms may be literally a matter of life and death. Many city dwellers are discovering what the pioneers taught long ago: each individual is responsible for the quality, and often the length, of his or her life. The grim legal facts are that by statute and court decree, local and stale governments and "their agents," the police, have no obligation to provide protection for the individual. These facts notwithstanding, for a police force to have the ability to watch over each of us night and day, to protect us from harm or crime, Americans would be forced to give up most of the freedoms that make life worth living in this great country. Freedom would literally be smothered by security, not infused with responsibility. Logically, if the police cannot protect each individual from crime, then every effort must be made to ensure that each citizen is capable of protecting himself or herself. The recent growth in citizen-police cooperation, best exemplified by 'Neighborhood Watch' programs, is an obvious manifestation of this reasonable crime control measure. Gun owners know that they are secure in their homes, capable of defending themselves and their families within the home and statistics and studies back this up. Outside of the home however, it is a different matter. Though the right to keep arms is widely recognized, though not totally honored, the right to bear arms has been under siege from anti-gunners for decades. In fact, most urban areas explicitly deny your right to carry a firearm concealed for self-protection. Most communities that restrict concealed carrying do so through laws that allow only certain occupational groups - like security guards - or the politically powerful elite to carry a weapon concealed for self-defense. But, in addition to using restrictive gun laws to discriminate against some classes of citizens, some powerful authorities, like the mayor of Gary, Indiana, use licensing laws to enact gun prohibition. In 1980, Mayor Richard Hatcher told his acting chief of police to quit distributing applications for handgun permits from police headquarters. Although no policy was ever announced for for not accept application for permits, citizens were unable find the application forms at any other location. More than 2,000 citizens of Gary sued the mayor and the chief of police. This group included businessmen who needed permits to carry handguns because they traveled around the city with large amounts of money, a security guard, an attorney and other homeowners. The mayor's action effectively denied this group of citizens any choice in the crucial decision of whether or not to carry a concealed weapon for self-protection. Three years later, a jury awarded the citizens $880,000 in damages and $524,000 in legal fees and costs. NRA-ILA provided financial help in the case and filed an amicus curiae brief new pending before the 3rd District Court of Appeals of Indiana. Though the mayor and the other defendants appealed this decisions, that court case represented a significant -- albeit costly -- victory for gun owners. That's why NRA-ILA has chosen to wage battle, where necessary, in defense of your full Second Amendment rights, to enact legislation to preclude antigun schemes similar to Mayor Hatcher's. The "model" legislation would ensure that permits are issued in a swift, fair and impartial manner, after a criminal records check has deemed an applicant to be qualified. The burden for proof would shift from the honest citizen seeking the permit to the licensing authority. Even as you read this, a battle is being fought in the state of Utah to bring some sanity back into the laws governing firearm ownership and use. And recently, gun owns owners came within a "veto" of enacting a comprehensive concealed carry permit law in Florida, which would have restored Second Amendment right to the residents of that state. Despite overwhelming support in both houses of the Florida state legislature and despite an aggressive campaign by the Unified Sportsmen of Florida - and Director Marion Hammer - Gov. Bob Graham vetoed the bill. The battle is far from over, in fact, it has just begun. It is NRA-ILA's goal to ensure that every proven, law-abiding and responsible individual who wants to carry a handgun for protection, who feels the need to be ready lo defend him or herself, be able to do so without being made a criminal by unfair, unnecessary and restrictive anti-gun laws. In conjunction with the legislative campaign, NRA's Voluntary Practical Firearms Program continues to offer expert training to the law-abiding citizen in the safe handling of handguns for personal and family protection. For a listing of loyal NRA Certified Instructors, contact the NRA Voluntary Practical Firearms Dept., 1600 Rhode Island Ave. NW, Washington DC 20036.

If you want to see how public opinion poll politics really work, take a look at who's suddenly talking tough about crime. Back in November, Bill Clinton walked softly around the "Three Strikes You're Out" life-sentencing mandate NRA pushed to victory in Washington state. But now he's Johnny-On-The-Spot while national TV cameras roll, taking a page directly out of NRA's book and claiming the credit. You can call that what you'd like, but I'll stick to Johnny-Come-Lately. Neither Clinton nor anyone on his staff championed criminal justice reform before NRA rammed through tough anti-crime wins in the last general elections. Now, the polls point toward crime as America's number one issue. And that's precisely what NRA has tried to tell anyone who cared enough to listen. Someone who hasn't been listening is the President's very own chief law enforcement official, Janet Reno. While NRA fought for juvenile justice reform, Reno tried to place the blame for gang violence and other mayhem conducted by predatory teens on semi-autos. And when NRA lined up squarely behind harsh mandatory sentences for anyone who used a gun to commit a crime, the Attorney General backpedaled. In fact, she told her prosecutors to sidestep tough federal sentencing through the use of plea bargaining. So, when the echo from all the finger banging fades away, will the American people really think that Bill Clinton has led the charge against criminal violence? Not unless his spin doctors can work black magic. Because the public at large and NRA have been way out in front on this issue, and we were there long before Bill Clinton said his last goodbyes to Little Rock. Not that the President hasn't had his chances. When America asked for a tough new brand of crime reform, the President tossed them a piece of nonsense called the Brady bill - legislation so baffling that police can't figure on how to enforce it. So once again we get symbolism over substance from our commander in chief, while NRA keeps working to keep violent felons in prison. That's the difference between real leadership, and just another Johnny-Come-Lately.

S.3 is the cryptic symbol which in the future will designate U. S. Senate Bill No. 3, introduced by Senators Copeland, Vandenberg, and Murphy (the Senate Racketeering Committee), to regulate the manufacture and distribution of firearms in the United States. S. 3 is something of a history-making bill, being the first Federal Firearms Bill ever introduced which strikes directly at the criminal and the criminal alone. S. 3 is also the first Federal Firearms Bill introduced after exhaustive hearings which gave police, prosecuting officials, active jurists, social workers, sportsmen, and friends of national defense an equal opportunity to be heard. In brief, S. 3 provides that manufacturers and dealers in firearms and ammunition must be licensed by the Secretary of Commerce. The cost is one dollar for a dealer and one hundred dollars for a manufacturer. The license does not need to be renewed annually, but will remain in effect during the good behavior of the licensee. All such manufacturers and dealers must then maintain a register of sales so that arms may be traced from the manufacturer to the purchaser. The bill prohibits interstate transportation and importation of any machine gun, with the proper exceptions for military and police units. It prohibits the interstate transportation of a firearm by any person under indictment or who has been convicted of a crime of violence, or who is a fugitive from justice. It prohibits the interstate transportation of stolen firearms, and the pawning of such firearms. It prohibits the interstate transportation of firearms on which the manufacturer's serial number has been altered or obliterated. S. 3 can easily be supported by state legislation invoking the police powers which are available to the state but not to the Federal Government, so as to completely prohibit the possession of firearms and ammunition by criminals, mental incompetents, vagrants, and other undesirables. With such legislation in the various states prohibiting possession, and with S. 3 on the Federal statutes prohibiting transportation, the police network around the armed criminal would be complete- and the ability of the sportsman to enjoy firearms, and the right of the home-owner and small merchant to protect their personal property would not be impaired. This is the end toward which all organized sportsmen should work. Members of the National Rifle Association should immediately communicate with Senator Copeland and his colleagues of the Racketeering Committee, Senators Vandenberg and Murphy, expressing appreciation for the constructive work which they have done in drafting S. 3. Members should also communicate with their own United States Senators and Congressmen, expressing approval of S. 3 in its present form, and urging support for this measure in the Senate and House of Representatives. Immediate action is essential. If we are to prevent the adoption of a type of Federal Firearms Bill which we do not like, we must secure the adoption of the kind of Federal Bill that we can support. It is just as important that you register your support of S. 3 with your Senator and Congressman as it was for you to register your opposition to the Keenan proposals at the last Congress. S. 3 sets a new plane for sane firearms regulation in this country. Support it actively and immediately.

In the coming months America's major metropolitan newspapers will he running a series of ads sponsored by the NRA - some of you in selected areas may have seen them already. The ads are a departure from our other advertising campaigns. And due to their graphic no nonsense treatment of violent crime they are bound to create controversy. We are running these ads for a very important reason. The time has arrived for all Americans to face facts about violent crime. It is also time for Americans to remember they have a constitutional right to protect themselves. Questions about self defense and gun ownership have stirred up a stream of philosophical debate during the past several years. Yet crime - violent life-shattering, heinous crime - strikes without regard to personal beliefs about firearms ownership. Crime preys upon liberals and conservatives alike. It destroys both the rich and the poor. It knows no age limit. Crime has no respect for gender. Faced with the cruel reality of criminal assault, your philosophy no longer counts. Your survival does. The NKA has never insisted that any American own a gun. As we have said in the past and will repeatedly say again: don't own a firearm if you choose not to. But never let any one deny or delay your constitutional freedom to make that choice. Unfortunately there are others who would take that choice away. You're probably aware that groups like Handgun Control Inc are lobbying across the nation, using every tactic at their disposal to deny you your right to purchase a handgun for self-defense. Yet, all the time our opponents are attacking the NRA for defending America's Second Amendment rights, we are deluged by statistics and headlines indicating crime is on an upsurge in America, and that the very nature of these cranes is growing more violent day by day. Did you know that a 20-year-old American female now has a 72% chance of being raped, robbed or assaulted during her lifetime? Did you realize that violent crime has grown to such proportions that it often takes the police over an hour to respond? Did you know 650,000 Americans thwart criminal attack with privately owned handguns each year? Americans, frustrated with the brutality of crime and the inability of our legal system to cope with it, are growing aware of their responsibility to defend themselves. At the same time anti-gunners are proclaiming that denying our right to own firearms is the only answer to violent crime. The gun control forces are steadfast in their smugness. Outlaw guns and criminals won't have them, they say. Outlaw guns and all problems will magically disappear. But the criminals themselves say they can sidestep gun control laws just like they sidestep other laws. They laugh and say gun control laws affect only the law-abiding. Obviously they are right. Gun control laws have already been enacted throughout our country and in every instance crime rates in these places continued to grow. Statistics back us up but our new ad campaign isn't just talking about statistics. Instead we're focusing on the actual emotional and physical anguish of crime victims. We want to make Americans aware of how a convenience store clerk must feel facing execution at the hands of a criminal. We want people to realize that throughout this country our elderly fear violent muggings not only in the streets  but in their own homes. We want the world to know that women are being terrorized and violated by thugs. Most of all, we want everyone to realize that they have a constitutional and god given right to protect themselves and their families. The police can't mount a 24 hour vigil at your home or business. They can't constantly patrol all the parks and backstreets. Handgun Control, Inc. won't be there to defend you. Yet there is another choice. You can purchase a firearm and learn how to use if for self-defense. No one can make that choice for you. But we will fight for your right to have that choice. We'll take a lot flak over the gutty impact of our new ad campaign. Our opponents will claim we're using scare tactics, reverting to sensationalism, preying upon the fear now spreading throughout society. These ads will make gun control groups nervous, as well they should. They'll grow nervous because they cannot dispute the truth. These ads did not evolve from  fiction. Instead, they sprang from the newspaper headlines and the television news footage that streams out at us every day. These ads are substantiated by U.S. Department of Justice findings. They are underscored by testimony from actual hardened criminals. They are the real life shattering nightmares of real, everyday people; hundreds of thousands of American citizens just like you and me. This is the real story about crime in America. The haunting story of how our friends and neighbors are humiliated, terrorized, their peace and tranquility torn asunder. It is the story of the victim, not the criminal; the story that gets buried on page 16 in your local newspaper. The story that anyone with a conscience cannot ignore. Think about this? What it your daughter was awakened in her sleep by a knife-wielding rapist? Would you want her to own and know how to use a handgun? Did you know that only 3% of rape attempts are completed against armed victims? What if your son, working his way through college at a convenience store, was told by an armed robber to kneel down in a storage room? This is the reality of law-abiding gun ownership; this is the truth about self-defense. Our new ad campaign may be shocking to some. But even more shocking is the truth it portrays. Don't own a gun if you don't choose to. But before anyone condemns gun ownership, maybe they should remember the victims. Many would like lo still be alive to have that choice.

IN THIS issue we carry for the first time a full page devoted to brief summaries of coming events in the rifle and pistol-shooting world. This year for the first time in three years the National Matches are to be resumed. Programs are already out or are being prepared for all the established tournaments, and many new ones are being added. Entries in the Spring Postal Matches exceed those of last year by an encouraging amount. On all sides there is definite evidence that the 1935 outdoor season will establish new records for interest and attendance at organized, supervised shooting matches. Rifle and pistol-shooting has proven itself to be an almost depression-proof sport. This has been particularly true of the .22-caliber rifle and pistol game. It is accordingly not surprising that as soon as the first shadows of the depression begin to lift, the sport of rifle and pistol-shooting should immediately show signs of tremendous forward movement. Once again the value of a strong National Association is thus demonstrated. While local clubs have found the going hard, have in many cases been forced to "give up the ghost"; while State Associations have in many cases become inactive even though maintaining a skeleton organization, the National Association has been able to carry on with national and regional competitions to maintain and stimulate interest, has continually carried on a campaign of education pointing to the possibilities of rifle and pistol-shooting as a wholesome sport, has proceeded with the organization of new clubs to take the place of those which have fallen by the wayside, has prevented the passage of numerous anti-firearms bills which would have increased the difficulty of promoting the sport as "times get better," and has finally succeeded in persuading Congress of the wisdom of re-establishing the National Matches just at a time when the incentive provided by the National Matches will be of the greatest value in bringing old-timers back into the fold and in publicizing the sport for newcomers. There are those who in their unselfish devotion to the interests of their local clubs and State Associations sometimes lose sight of the essential part in the promotion of the shooting game which is played by the National Association. The individual paying his dues to the local club sometimes wonders why he should also support the National Association. The story which is told by the full-page listing of coming events in this issue-the story of a renaissance definitely and noticeably under way in our sport at a time when many other activities are still wondering when the depression will be over, is the answer. The loyalty of individuals, clubs, and State Associations to the national organization during the past three trying years is being repaid in the program of activities for the coming summer. Rifle and pistol shooters may well turn to their hobby and recreation with renewed interest, renewed confidence, and renewed enthusiasm. They may well rededicate themselves under the leadership of the National Rifle Association to the task of making America once again a Nation of Riflemen. Forward, Riflemen!

THE GREATEST trouble with wildlife conservation in America today is that it is a rich man's job. That, or a job which can be done only with the help of a sizable Federal or state appropriation. Even with the aid of the Pittman-Robertson act and the nine million dollars it will give this year toward the conservation of America's game supply, these appropriations are pitifully inadequate to the job of guaranteeing future sport for the twelve or thirteen million who will go hunting this fall. Individually, in their role as conscientious hunters, America's outdoorsmen can't seem to do much toward helping our conservation agencies in the job of maintaining the game supply. They can't personally protect the deer population of their state, or even of their own county. They can't buy up land for use as a wildlife refuge. They feel unable to take the place of Federal or state wardens. They doubt their ability even to take a hand when a member of their own party breaks the law by killing a doe "for camp meat." They stand alone, it seems - men with licenses, guns, and a love of the outdoors - while somebody else figures out the laws, tries to enforce them, and arranges for the appropriations. It is unpleasant to think about, but the fact remains that much of our conservation effort is directed, not at a positive approach to the problem of sound game management, but against the irresponsibility of the sportsman himself. Conservation agencies spend their time, and much of their pitifully small budgets, in forcing the sportsman to stay within laws which were designed to safeguard his hunting "privileges." Game conservation is becoming a policeman's job. It has no business turning into such a law-enforcement body. The tragic part of it is that we might all but wipe out the need for enforcement of our conservation program, and use those appropriations purely for game research projects, if the individual "sportsman" would do his share of the job. Practically every enemy of abundant game could be critically weakened if sportsmen paid more than lip service to the rules of their sport. Consider, for instance, the strangely misguided sense of fair play which allows a "good" sportsman to observe to the letter his own ideas of game conservation and yet wink at the malpractices of his fellow hunter. How often do we hear that someone killed a doe by mistake, and once the error was made, cut it up for camp use. You wouldn't make the mistake in the first place. And if you had, you would be good sport enough to call it your deer for the season and not go after another. But, because someone else did it, and not you, you wink at the whole affair. You don't even put up an argument when he goes after a "legal" deer that he can take out on his license. That kind of sportsmanship is neither sporting nor good sense. It is like letting a man get away when you've just watched him break into a grocery store and clean out the cash register. It is poor sportsmanship, and poor business. So conservation is like everything else, after all. It boils down to a miserable failure of the "let Joe do it" theory. Joe, personified in this case by Federal and state agencies, will try to do it, but he can't begin to do it all. He can't get far with about 60 federal wardens, for instance, and a few million dollars for the whole program. And when a share of that tiny appropriation must be spent guarding the game supply against the "sportsman," in order to have any game left at all. The problem is out of hand.
